claims.text: The untreated TiVNbTa baseline is a single-phase BCC dendritic alloy.
Untreated TiVNbTa has a yield strength of approximately 330 MPa at 1273 K.
Untreated TiVNbTa has a compressive strength of approximately 423 MPa at 1273 K.
Untreated TiVNbTa has approximately 40% strain ductility at 1273 K.
The proposed intervention is addition of 0.5–1 wt% Y2O3 nanoparticles to TiVNbTa.
Mechanical alloying under inert atmosphere, HIP at approximately 900 °C, and aging will produce a homogeneous nanoscale Y2O3 dispersion.
The modified material will contain uniformly distributed nanoscale Y2O3 particles embedded in its BCC matrix.
Dispersed Y2O3 particles will pin dislocations in TiVNbTa.
Dispersed Y2O3 particles will stabilize grain boundaries in TiVNbTa.
The oxide dispersion will inhibit grain coarsening at high temperature.
The oxide dispersion will inhibit dislocation motion at high temperature.
Dispersion strengthening will increase the 1273 K yield strength by at least 20% relative to 330 MPa.
Dispersion strengthening will increase the 1273 K compressive strength by at least 20% relative to 423 MPa.
The modified alloy will retain a strain capacity of at least 30% at 1273 K.
The modified alloy will avoid a greater than 10% reduction in ductility relative to untreated TiVNbTa.
The modified alloy will avoid a greater than 10% reduction in thermal conductivity relative to untreated TiVNbTa.
The retained thermal conductivity will be adequate for efficient heat transfer between W and CuCrZr.
The proposed improvements will persist at temperatures up to 1273 K.
The proposed improvements will persist under loading conditions relevant to plasma-facing divertor applications.

contradictions.description: The predicted outcome permits ductility as low as 30%, but a greater than 10% loss from the stated 40% baseline would trigger falsification, requiring ductility of at least about 36%. Thus, results between 30% and 36% would simultaneously satisfy the stated performance prediction and falsify the hypothesis.
The hypothesis says ductility will not be compromised, whereas the quantified prediction allows a decline from the stated 40% baseline to 30%, a 25% reduction.
